questions.rawText:
A)
Design a combinational circuit using programmable logic array (PLA) to implement a full subtractor.

B)
Construct a Mod-10 ripple up-counter using negative edge triggered T flip-flops and draw the output
timing diagrams.

C)
Write Verilog dataflow code to implement 8:1 multiplexer without using the instances of 2:1
multiplexers.

A)
Design a 3-bit self-correcting synchronous counter using JK flip-flops that follows the sequence 7-6-
4-3 repeatedly, ensuring that any unused states automatically go to the state-7 on the next clock
pulse.

B)
Explain the Time Division Multiple Access bus arbitration protocol.

C)
With an example, explain the role of instances in Verilog programming.

A)
Design a Mealy synchronous sequential circuit using D flip-flops with a serial input x and output z
that produces z = 1 whenever the input completes the sequence 1011. Overlapping is allowed.

B)
Use the Booth's algorithm to multiply +23 (multiplicand) by -10 (multiplier), where each number is
represented using 6 bits.

C)
Write a behavioral Verilog code for a 4:1 MUX using an "always block" and "case statement".

A)
Analyze the sequential circuit shown below and obtain its state table and state diagram.

B)
Express the given statement in three, two and one instruction addressing formats: D = A + B×C

C)
What is the difference between non-pipelined and pipelined processors? If the number of stages is
6 and instructions to be executed are 5, how many cycles for execution are required in both cases?

A)
A mod-6 asynchronous up-counter using negative edge triggered T flip-flops, which resets itself if
any undesired state occurs needs to be designed. Write the Verilog code to implement the same.

B)
Define the following addressing modes with an example for each type:
(i) register-indirect, (ii) displacement, (iii) autodecrement, (iv) implied (implicit)

C)
Explain the operation of accumulator-based computer organization.
